Chapter 7: The Power and Limits of Activism
You know, activism usually starts with a spark—a moment when you just can’t look away from what’s wrong in the world. But turning that spark into real change? That’s a journey, and it’s not an easy one. There are setbacks. Small wins. And honestly, a constant tug-of-war between hope and disappointment.
Picture this: a group of neighbors, tired of skyrocketing rents and endless evictions, start gathering in a church basement. They share stories—some heartbreaking—about families forced to move over and over again. At first, it feels like nothing’s changing. City officials listen, nod politely, and then... nothing happens. The group thinks about quitting, but the need is just too big to ignore.
At the same time, there’s a high school student, watching climate protests online, feeling inspired. She decides to organize a walkout at her school. She figures maybe a few friends will join in, but when the day comes? Dozens of students show up—homemade signs in hand, chanting for change. The principal threatens them with detention, but no one backs down. Instead, they feel this surge of energy, this sense of standing together.
Most people never see what goes on behind the scenes—the hours spent in endless meetings, the petitions that gather dust, the moments when hope feels almost too heavy to carry. Activism isn’t glamorous. It’s made up of tiny, stubborn acts that are often met with indifference—or even outright hostility.
But here’s the thing: the real power of activism doesn’t always show up in big headlines or sweeping victories. It’s found in the simple act of coming together. Even when change is slow, organizing as a group builds community, teaches new skills, and proves to everyone involved that they’re not facing these struggles alone.
It’s easy to get stuck thinking that only the big wins matter. But the truth is, real change usually comes in small, uneven steps.
Those neighbors? They kept meeting—over time, they managed to win a small grant to help support tenants’ rights. The student’s protest? It didn’t change the world overnight, but it did spark new conversations in her district and led to fresh environmental initiatives.
No, these weren’t earth-shattering transformations. But to the people involved, they meant the world. Standing up, refusing to accept things as they are—that leaves a mark, one that sticks long after the news coverage fades away.
